To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a synthetic, nonanticoagulant polyanionic aromatic molecule (RG-13578) mimics the functional properties of heparin in modulating FGF-2 receptor binding and signal transduction.

a synthetic, nonsulphated polyanionic compound (RG-13 557) inhibits the binding of FGF- 2 to soluble and cell surface FGFR1, abrogates heparin-induced FGF-2 dimerization and FGFR1 tyrosine phosphoryl ation, and prevents FGF-2 induced endothelial cell proliferation and angiogenesis.
a synthetic, nonsulphated polyanionic compound (RG- 13577) inhibits FGF-2 receptor binding and dimerization, and abrogates FGF-2 signaling and angiogenic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of the angiogenic effects of FGF-1 and FGF-1 by heparin-m imicking compounds, such as RG-13577.
the development and evaluation of novel polyanionic compounds as inhibitors of angiogenesis.
the role of heparan sulfate (HS)/proteoglycans in the regulation of cell growth induced by basic fibrolblast growth factor (bFGF) and other heprin-binding growth factors (HBGFs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
compound RG-135777 is a potent antagonist of the FGF-2 signaling pathway and that this effect may be mediated by its ability to interfere with the FGF-1 and FGF-1 receptor interactions.

the compound RG-1357, a non-sulfated, non-heparin-like polyanionic compound, inhibits the mitogenic activity of FGF- 2 by blocking the interaction with the FGF-2 receptor, the dimerization of the receptor, and the signal transduction pathway.
the compound RG-1357 inhibits the biological activity of FGF- 2 by preventing its interaction with the FGFR1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RG-13577 mimics some of the functional activities of HS and, in particular, heparin.
the synthetic polyanion RG-13577 inhibits FGF-2-mediated cell proliferation and angiogenesis by interfering with FGF-2 receptor binding and dimerization.
RG-13577 mimics the HS-mediated effects of FGF-1/2 on FGFR1 and FGFR2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthetic polyanionic compound, RG-1357, is a heparin/ HS mimetic that inhibits angiogenesis and FGF- 2 signaling.
a nonsulfated polycationic compound, RG-13578, mimics functional features associated with HS and inhibits FGF-2 signaling and angiogenesis.
a synthetic polyanionic compound, RG-135777, can inhibit FGF- 2-induced angiogenesis by interfering with FGF-2/FGFR1 interaction.
